description: Applies to repositories containing CLI code.

notAuthoritativeFor: Non-CLI repositories, operations, deployment, or project behavior.

dos: These conventions apply to repositories containing CLI application code.
CLI application repositories must also apply application.json.
donts: CLI application repositories must not omit application.json or applicable CLI requirements.

dos: Every CLI repository must extend the general AGENTS.md requirements with applicable CLI guidance.
donts: A CLI repository must not omit AGENTS.md.

dos: After the seven general AGENTS.md headings, add a ## CLI section. Document each executable entrypoint and its target; command/subcommand names; option and positional-argument parsing, defaults, validation, forwarding, and errors; exit-code meanings and mapping; supported platforms and platform-specific behavior; --help and --version behavior; and destructive-action safeguards such as dry-run, confirmation, and scope limits. Include applicable validation commands.
donts: AGENTS.md must not leave CLI entrypoints or required CLI validation undefined.

dos: CLI applications must contain bin/ with the executable entrypoint, implement and document --help and --version, document exit codes and redacted output, and provide dry-run or confirmation controls for destructive actions.
donts: CLI applications must not omit bin/, --help, --version, or required safety controls, or expose secrets.

dos: CLI README.md must add Commands and Exit codes, in that order, documenting installation, each user-facing command and important options, --help, --version, safe copyable examples, supported platform behavior, exit-code meanings, and destructive-action controls. Place these headings in the profile extension area defined by general.json and include them in the Table of Contents.
donts: Do not show destructive commands without dry-run, confirmation, or equivalent safety behavior, and do not claim platform support that is not validated.
